speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I wish to declare my interest as Co-Chairperson of the Financial Sector Tripartite Committee (FSTC) which was launched a fortnight ago as part of the national SkillsFuture initiative.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Building a ready, resilient and relevant financial sector workforce is of importance because the financial sector is a strong contributor to our economic growth, our productivity growth and our growing influence and impact as a regional and global financial hub and centre.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This is further accentuated by the fact that the sector is powered by a 170,000-strong workforce and whose productivity is one of the highest across various sectors and where Professionals, Managers and Executives (PMEs) form the majority of the workforce.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: All the recent announcements about layoffs, wage freezes and lacklustre performance of global banking giants in the financial sector have fuelled global and local fears, uncertainties and doubts in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This is further exacerbated by the plunge in crude oil prices, currency fluctuations and stock markets at new lows in the first two months of this year which all have ripple effects on the financial sector, whether it is demand on banking, finance, insurance, asset management services as well as stresses on loans and loan repayments.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: National retrenchment figures have also crept up in 2015, compared with 2014.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: At the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), we are also seeing more PMEs from the financial sector visit our U PME Centre to seek assistance since the last quarter of 2015.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In Singapore alone, Standard Chartered employs 7,000 workers, many of whom are Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In January, Barclays also had to let go some of its employees as part of its move to exit the global institutional cash equities, equity research and equities capital market businesses.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In fact, two weeks ago, I met up with 10 of those who were retrenched in January.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Why is this happening in the financial sector?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: There are many answers to that question: too rapid expansion; too high cost of manpower and rent; restructuring and recalibration; product consolidation, hence, the closure of major product lines; technological disruption of financial technology (fintech) and the overall global economic outlook.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Page: 113 These are just some of the reasons why foreign financial institutions are hitting rough patches.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Staying ready, resilient and relevant involves not just individuals and workers per se but includes our unions, employers, the Government, regulators and key stakeholders partnering in the journey.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: What do we mean by "ready"? "Ready" means that we are prepared for anything that comes our way.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: It also means we can change and adapt in fluid, volatile, new and changing environment and circumstances.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: It does not mean that a person does not experience difficulty or distress but that he or she has the power and ability to "bounce back" and recover quickly after weathering any challenges or adversity. "Relevant" means staying abreast and even ahead of current developments and possessing the needed skills, learning and mindset to remain updated, current and both employed and employable.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How to build a 3R workforce in the financial sector?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Building a ready, resilient and relevant workforce – a 3R workforce – requires beyond individual efforts to collective efforts by every individual and each of the tripartite partners.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: NTUC's Financial and Business Services cluster of unions recently ran a series of focus group sessions and engaged more than 100 employees working in the financial sector from various financial institutions and in various job roles and grades.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Workers and unions all agree that the financial sector landscape is changing rapidly.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: New jobs are being created with the advent of digital age and disruptive technology.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: They are what are now called 3G jobs; "3G" meaning "going, going, gone".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Workers in this sector need to stay proactive and positive.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Proactive to upskill to move up and stay ahead.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Proactive to reskill if old jobs are gone and new technology and ways of doing things are introduced.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Proactive to second-skill themselves in case they need to move out or across to a new job.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Positive to embrace change, stay in control and ahead of the challenges coming their way and overcome any adversity.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: We want to ensure careers do not plateau because workers have stopped growing, stopped learning and stopped adapting.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Unions, too, need to support, assist and encourage fellow workers and secure a positive environment and system for the worker to stay employed and employable.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: During this time of economic restructuring and transformation and amidst cyclical and structural challenges, besides ensuring that workers in this sector are protected and represented, unions need to strive to stay relevant, progressive and ahead in light of the changing workforce profile and employment landscape.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many in this sector are not aware of the latest and upcoming changes to 	Page: 114 labour legislation and that PMEs, too, can be union members and enjoy the protection and the entire host of services which NTUC and our affiliated unions can provide.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In the same vein, employers in the financial sector play a vital role in building a 3R workforce.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: It is imperative for employers to ensure they are progressive in practice and create progression pathways and build the Singaporean Core.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Employers need to pay close attention to training, exposure and coaching to equip workers with skills to advance to better jobs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Employers need to motivate and empower more uptake of training opportunities.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Employers also need to provide a clear progression path upward for employees who develop and demonstrate skills, capabilities and competencies.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: After all, younger, less experienced staff are cheaper to retain on the payroll.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: These displaced mature PMEs above 40 have families and children to support.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How is Singapore to develop a resilient core of local talent if the first in line to be retrenched are these mature PMEs, ostensibly because the ones at the top making the decision are anxious to protect their own jobs?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Have banks adequately considered the additional risk they potentially face by letting go experienced staff?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Amount of retrenchment benefits to be paid to PMEs?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How much notice must I give the worker or union?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: These are questions I hope employers, in particular, those non-unionised ones, will give serious thought to and be fair and progressive in their practices.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many global businesses are creating jobs of the future at breakneck pace and we need to ensure that Singaporean employees in the financial sector have the right skills to fill them.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: If you are ready to work, you should be able to find a job that fits your skills.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: And if you want to move up within your field into a better job, you should have access to training to get the skills you need.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: For the financial sector, as many are global companies not based in Singapore, to take on bigger roles, we need to provide the much needed regional and international exposure and not just skills alone.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The Government plays a vital role in minimising job mismatch, skills mismatch and expectation mismatch.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many of the curricula in finance courses in polytechnics and universities do not really teach banking.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: We should link our Pre-Employment Training courses with in depth Continuing Education and Training (CET) programmes so that our talent can be job-ready even before they enter the industry.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, if finance majors intend to build a career in banking, their internships should be coupled with certification programmes whilst attached to banks and learn as they earn, and not just limited to polytechnic but also for university students, and taking certification programmes with financial training institutes which are currently 	Page: 115 offering CET programmes.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many of our banking talent, too, have become specialists and not given the opportunity to learn about other areas in banking.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: They are not encouraged to move through different areas or departments.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I believe we should have an adult "Earn and Learn" as well.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Give our local talent the opportunities to be attached or move across different areas of banking – front office, middle office and back office.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: And if there are opportunities to take on short-term global projects, do not just give to specialists to be posted for those overseas projects.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Let our local talent be given those overseas projects as well and gradually assimilate and progress into the job.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, with the current letting go of banking talent, can we redeploy the talent displaced to other areas and can they be given "Earn and Learn" opportunities as well?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: They can be sent for accredited programmes whilst being deployed in areas in the bank or other parts of the bank where they can be utilised.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: MAS, the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS), IBF, the Singapore Workforce Development Agency (WDA), U PME Centre and NTUC e2i (Employment and Employability Institute) will provide the expertise and resources to support FiCAC in its work.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: With the support of ABS and U PME Centre, FiCAC will also organise talks on job opportunities in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I urge our tripartite partners to leverage one another's strengths, continue to partner closely to drive our collective efforts for the sector and stay ahead of the game through innovation and shared goals.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Page: 116 It requires not just individual responsibility, proactiveness and initiative by our workers and unions but the conviction, commitment and tenacity of employers to develop their human capital and build a strong Singaporean Core; and finally, strong support, promotion and assistance from the Government, so that we stay on the right course of this journey.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: As one of the top financial hubs that thrive in the region, it is crucial for the Singapore financial sector workforce to remain relevant, resilient and ready so as to stay ahead of the competition.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The financial sector has to ensure that the workforce continues to enhance its competency level, capabilities and professionalism by acquiring work skills in new or developing business areas, or in developing more sophisticated or specialist skill-sets.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Only then can we effectively stay future-ready to serve markets not just locally, but regionally and globally.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As he mentioned, with sluggish growth in the global economy, coupled with ongoing implementation of the international regulatory reform measures, we are, indeed, seeing consolidation pressures in financial sectors all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I had mentioned just now, Singapore is not spared from these forces and consolidation pressures, but the impact on our financial sector has been relatively contained.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even as we see some retrenchments from certain banks, others continue to expand and hire.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why, as I said, we are still generating, on a net basis, new jobs in the finance sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also see demand for talent in key areas of finance, like asset and wealth management, insurance, compliance and risk management.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking ahead, we expect to see continued job creation in the financial sector, although at a more moderated pace than before.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the medium term, we have several plus points in our favour.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The strong pace of urbanisation in Asian cities will spur significant demand for infrastructure development and financing, as well as insurance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There will be growing affluence in Asia with the rising middle class, leading to increased demand for financial services.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as a key financial centre for the region, Singapore stands to benefit from these longer-term trends.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Financial institutions are also increasingly adopting new financial technology, or fintech.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Demand is growing for people with competencies in these areas, like cybersecurity, data analytics, application design and development, as well as network and infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are areas which Singaporeans can excel in, and secure potentially good jobs in the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS is working very closely with this tripartite committee, NTUC and the financial cluster unions to help and support those who are affected.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, individuals can approach a new one-stop career advisory facility for guidance relating to skills upgrading, and career opportunities 	Page: 117 in finance and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond immediate assistance to those who are affected, we also need to look ahead to the middle term to chart the future skills that are needed for the financial industry and systematically equip Singaporeans with these skills.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Patrick Tay had elaborated at length on this; I just want to comment briefly on three areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, as Mr Patrick Tay had suggested, we must get our basics right and make sure that our education system prepares our young people and our potential entrants to the financial sector well for the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Patrick Tay mentioned that banking is not taught in polytechnics and universities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I did a check – banking is covered in the modules and curriculums of polytechnics and universities, but I agree that the curriculum can be improved.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why MAS is working with the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to enhance the curriculum of existing banking and finance modules, including having more well-structured internships, at both the polytechnic and university levels.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will provide more learning pathways and training opportunities for Singaporean finance professionals at all levels to tap on the SkillsFuture measures and pursue mastery in their respective fields.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS is already doing this through various schemes under SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking ahead, we will collaborate with different stakeholders, including IBF and the unions, to review and develop additional programmes needed to upskill industry competencies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Patrick Tay had suggested that there may be too many of our banking professionals becoming specialists or taking on specialist roles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, in fact, we need many more Singaporean specialists, in areas like risk management, compliance, wealth management and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do need more people to go deeper into these specialist areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can do various things to nurture them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can set up new centres of excellence to deepen capabilities and work with employers to develop meaningful career progression for these specialists.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, while we provide for specialist skills in areas of need, I agree with Mr Patrick Tay that we also need to develop professionals with a sufficient breadth of skills to be flexible and resilient in times of change.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All these will support continual learning pathways under SkillsFuture and facilitate more seamless transitions for professionals across different areas 	Page: 118 of finance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is something that I have talked about in this House at the last Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I mentioned that MAS has been engaging the top leadership of key financial institutions in this area of strengthening the Singaporean Core in our financial sector workforce and ensuring fair employment practices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The response that we have received from the top leadership of our key financial institutions – many of whom, incidentally, are Singaporeans as well – has been positive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are supporting programmes for Singaporean professionals to be nurtured, for example, by enabling them to take up cross-functional roles within the bank or to take up international postings for better exposure.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are some of the broad areas that I thought I should highlight and comment on.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am sure the tripartite committee co-chaired by Mr Patrick Tay will be having more detailed deliberations to see how these plans can be enhanced and well implemented on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, perhaps, next time, Mr Tay can respond to his Adjournment Motion with specific recommendations from the tripartite committee on its plans to improve in many of these areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In summary, the Government is stepping up its efforts and Singaporean financial sector workers can look forward to many more new programmes through SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But at the end of the day, a lot of this work comes down to individual mindsets.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Everyone must be prepared to do his part.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Patrick Tay had highlighted correctly, the next decade will be both disruptive and transformative for financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will have a significant bearing on the scale and nature of financial sector jobs around the world, including in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this period of volatility and change, we must all embrace the desire to keep learning and improving ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must all have a greater sense of urgency towards reskilling, upskilling and acquiring new skills.
